lessonsIntro: No surf school teaches at White Park Bay, and the National Trust warns that the beach is unsafe for swimming because of rip currents.

text: White Park Bay is a wide, remote National Trust beach between Ballintoy and Portbradden. It's beautiful to walk, but both the National Trust and the council's tourism site state that it's unsafe for swimming because of dangerous rip currents. We couldn't find a surf school that brings lessons here, and there's no lifeguard cover listed. That makes it a beach for experienced surfers who can read conditions, not a place to learn.

If you want to learn, book a lesson on a lifeguarded beach nearby instead: Portrush schools teach at East Strand and West Strand, and Ballycastle has seasonal RNLI cover. Access to White Park Bay is down steep steps and slopes from a small, rough car park with no toilets. The Trust also warns of rockfall from the cliffs towards Portbradden, so only cross that way along the beach at low tide.

cards.label: Level
cards.title: Not for beginners
cards.text: No lessons, no lifeguards and known rip currents. Learn elsewhere first.

cards.label: Best time
cards.title: Only when you can read it
cards.text: No official source gives surf timing advice. Experienced surfers should check forecasts and tides before making the walk down.

cards.label: Watch out for
cards.title: Rips and rockfall
cards.text: The Trust says rip currents make it unsafe for swimming, and the cliff towards Portbradden is unstable.

hireIntro: There's no surf hire at White Park Bay or in Ballintoy that we could confirm, so bring your own kit or hire in Portrush.

text: Because there's no lifeguard cover and the Trust warns about rips, only come here with your own kit and the experience to use it. Water temperatures match the rest of the North Coast: around 13-16°C in late summer and 6-9°C by late February, so you'll want a 5/4mm or thicker with boots, gloves and a hood in winter. Carry everything down the steep path, as there are no facilities.

cards.label: Board
cards.title: Your own, if you're experienced
cards.text: This isn't a learner's beach, so bring the board you normally surf.

cards.label: Wetsuit
cards.title: 4/3mm in summer, 5/4mm+ in winter
cards.text: Sea temperature data for this stretch of coast shows roughly 13-16°C in August and 6-9°C in late February, with boots, gloves and hood advised in winter.

cards.label: Other craft
cards.title: Not advised
cards.text: With rip currents and no lifeguards, the Trust's warning applies to anyone going in the water.

shopsIntro: There are no surf shops at White Park Bay; the nearest confirmed surf shops are in Portrush.
shopsText: White Park Bay has no shops or toilets. We couldn't find a surf shop in Ballintoy, Bushmills or Ballycastle. The nearest confirmed surf shops are in Portrush, where Troggs on Main Street sells and hires boards and wetsuits, with a second store on Causeway Street.

lessons.q: Can I take a surf lesson at White Park Bay?
lessons.a: No school teaches here that we could find. The nearest lessons are in Portrush, at East Strand and West Strand.

lessons.q: Is it safe to swim or surf at White Park Bay?
lessons.a: The National Trust says the beach is unsafe for swimming because of dangerous rip currents, and no lifeguard service is listed.

lessons.q: Is White Park Bay good for beginners?
lessons.a: No. With rips, no lifeguards and no school, beginners are better off on a lifeguarded beach with a lesson.

hire.q: Can I hire a surfboard at White Park Bay?
hire.a: No. The nearest confirmed hire is Troggs in Portrush.

hire.q: Is there parking at White Park Bay?
hire.a: There's a small free National Trust car park with a rough surface and limited spaces. If it's full, the Trust asks you to come back another time.

shops.q: Where's the nearest surf shop to White Park Bay?
shops.a: Troggs in Portrush is the nearest surf shop we could confirm.
